gen-dafont-bloody-gf-kedebideri: Loud, round-bowled drama from Bloody, with a tall and friendly sans waiting just underneath it. But where Bloody grabs attention outright, Kedebideri keeps its rounded letters open and inviting.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-lexend-deca: Swagger over simplicity: Bloody leans on big round lowercase bowls for its commanding look. Lexend Deca does the opposite job, keeping one unshaded line that never swells across its whole sans-serif body.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-martel-sans: Martel Sans opens up every curve and holds a high mean line across each word. Martel Sans can stay modest in size, since Bloody already supplies the shouting with its big round bowls.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-matangi: Twine pressed flat, in a hefty lowercase: that is Matangi. Beneath the commanding Bloody headings, those rounded, open letters should read smoothly paragraph after paragraph, with a unit-width stroke throughout.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-michroma: Bloody comes in with commanding, big round lowercase bowls, while Michroma gives every letter a wide berth on both sides. Punchy bowls above, spacious tall-bodied sans below, and the page has two voices.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-montserrat-underlin: Big-bowled swagger: Bloody is made to command a line all by itself. Montserrat Underline, a plain sans, keeps its bowls uniform and hairline-free, so it stays readable at small sizes.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-nata-sans: Nata Sans builds its capitals from lines of one constant thickness. Nata Sans quietly keeps its wide-mouthed curves steady, whereas Bloody does its best work as the loud, round-bowled headline.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-nobile: Nobile keeps almost no gap between x-height and capitals, and its letter mouths stay open like an unjoined chalk arc. Shrink Bloody and its commanding bowls lose all their swagger.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-armenian: Noto Sans Armenian reads full and welcoming, its c, s and z standing tall and its round letters opening wide. Bloody commands the top, and this text stays easygoing line after line.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Noto Sans Bamum reads clean and modern, with big counters inside every small letter. Noto Sans Bamum stays quiet in sans-serif fashion while Bloody brings the big round lowercase bowls.
